# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Nell, you should definitely wear your white organdy,” Isolde firmly suggested.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0000 }

The east gable chamber held them both; beyond its walls lingered merely twilight—an exquisite twilight of yellowish-green beneath a cloudless, clear-blue expanse. Above the Whispering Wood hung a large round moon, which gradually intensified from a pale sheen to polished silver; the night air overflowed with delightful summer noises—the twitter of drowsy birds, capricious gusts of wind, and distant voices accompanied by laughter. However, within Nell’s chamber, the blind had been pulled down and the lamp turned on, because a significant dressing process was underway.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0001 }

The east gable bore little resemblance to how it had appeared four years earlier on that evening, when its starkness had chilled Nell to the very core of her soul with its unwelcoming coldness. Modifications had gradually taken place, with Thirza reluctantly tolerating them, to the point where it had become as charming and delicate a haven as any young woman might wish for.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0002 }

Although the pink-rose velvet carpet and pink silk drapes of Nell’s youth had failed to appear, her aspirations had evolved alongside her maturity, making it unlikely that she mourned their absence. A lovely matting concealed the floor, while light-green art muslin formed the curtains that muted the tall window and moved in the stray gusts of wind. Rather than gold and silver brocade tapestry, a charming apple-blossom wallpaper covered the walls, which featured a handful of fine prints presented to Nell by Mrs. Wace. The position of prominence was held by Miss Thorne’s portrait, beneath which Nell made a tender ritual of placing blooming blossoms on the shelf. On this evening, a stalk of white lilies subtly scented the chamber like a remembered aroma. No “mahogany furniture” was present, yet the room contained a white-painted bookshelf stocked with volumes, a padded wicker rocking chair, a dressing table adorned with white muslin ruffles, an unusual mirror with a gilded frame topped by a curved apex painted with plump pink Cupids and purple grapes—which had previously belonged in the guest bedroom—and a low-built white bed.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0003 }

Nell was getting dressed because she was going to a concert at the Pale Sands Hotel. To assist the Port Marlow hospital, the guests had organized the event and had searched for every accessible amateur performer in the neighboring regions to contribute. A duet was requested from Bertha Sampson and Pearl Clay, who belonged to the Pale Sands Baptist choir; a violin solo was scheduled to be performed by Milton Clark of Stonebridge; a Scotch ballad was going to be sung by Winnie Adella Blair of Delford; and recitations were to be delivered by Laura Tranter of Tullyvale alongside Nell Harcourt of Brierley.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0004 }

Just as Nell used to remark, the event marked “an epoch in her life,” and the sheer thrill of it left her delightfully electrified. Obed experienced supreme bliss from the sense of pride in the distinction given to his Nell, while Thirza felt almost as much delight, even if she would have perished before acknowledging it, claiming that she deemed it quite inappropriate for a group of youngsters to go roaming off to the hotel lacking an adult to supervise them.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0005 }

A double-seated buggy driven by Odette Pullen and her brother Barney was going to carry Nell and Isolde; moreover, various other Brierley girls and boys were attending as well. Out from town, a group of visitors was anticipated, and following the concert, the performers were to be served a supper.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0006 }

“Is the organdy truly going to be the finest choice?” Nell asked in an anxious manner. “My blue-flowered muslin seems prettier to me—and this one is definitely not as stylish.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0007 }

“However, it fits you far better,” Isolde remarked. “It is very soft, frilled, and body-hugging. That muslin is rigid, giving you an overly formal appearance. Yet it appears as though the organdy developed naturally upon you.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0008 }

Nell let out a sigh and gave in. Isolde was starting to become known for her remarkable taste in attire, making her counsel on these matters highly desirable. On this specific evening, she looked quite attractive in a gown of that charming wild-rose pink, a shade from which Nell was permanently excluded; however, because she had no role in the concert, how she looked mattered less. Her entire effort was focused on Nell, whom she swore had to be attired, groomed, and decorated to suit the Regent’s liking for the sake of Brierley.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0009 }

“ Tug that frill out slightly further—like that; come here and allow me to fasten your sash; now we shall attend to your slippers. My plan is to weave your hair into a pair of heavy plaits, securing them midway up using large white ribbons—stop, do not draw even one curl onto your brow—leave only the gentle parting. No other hairstyle you wear flatters you to the same degree, Nell, and Mrs. Wace remarks that your appearance resembles a Madonna whenever it is parted in this manner. I am going to pin this tiny white house rose right behind your ear. My bush bore merely a single blossom, which I preserved on your behalf.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0010 }

“Would it be all right if I wore my pearl beads?” Nell inquired. “A string of them was brought to me from town by Obed last week, and I am certain he would enjoy seeing me wear them.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0011 }

Isolde pressed her lips together, tilted her dark head thoughtfully to evaluate the options, and ultimately chose the beads, which were subsequently fastened about the slender, alabaster neck of Nell.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0012 }

“You have such a stylish quality, Nell,” Isolde remarked, admiring her without envy. “The way you carry your head gives you quite an air. My guess is it comes from your figure. Me, I am merely a dumpling. It has been a constant fear of mine, and now my suspicion is confirmed. Oh well, I guess I must simply accept it.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0013 }

“However, you possess such dimples,” spoken by Nell, who smiled fondly into the lovely, lively face that was close to her. “Charming dimples, similar to small depressions in cream. I have abandoned any expectation of dimples. My dream of having dimples will not be realized; yet a great number of my dreams have been fulfilled, so I should not protest. Am I completely prepared now?”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0014 }

“Everything is prepared,” Isolde stated when Thirza stepped into the threshold, appearing as a lean form whose hair was more silvered than before and whose sharp contours remained, though her expression was considerably gentler. “Walk straight inside and see our reciter, Thirza. Is she not beautiful?”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0015 }

Thirza produced a noise that fell somewhere between a grunt and a sniff.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0016 }

“Her appearance is tidy and respectable. That hairstyle of hers appeals to me. However, she will probably spoil that gown while traveling over there through the dust and dampness, plus it seems almost overly light for such chilly evenings. Organdy is absolutely the most impractical material imaginable, a point I expressed to Obed when he purchased it. Yet talking to Obed these days serves no purpose. There was a period when he listened to my counsel, but currently he merely purchases items for Nell without care, and the Delford shop employees realize they can sell him whatever they wish. If they simply inform him that an item is attractive and stylish, Obed surrenders his cash instantly for it. Make certain your skirt stays away from the wheel, Nell, and wear your heavy coat.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0017 }

Afterward, Thirza marched down the stairs, reflecting with pride on how charming Nell appeared, featuring that
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0018 }

“One ray of moonshine extending from the forehead unto the crown”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0019 }

and feeling regret that she was unable to attend the concert in person to listen to her daughter's recitation.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0020 }

“I wonder whether my dress will suffer from the dampness,” Nell remarked with concern.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0021 }

“Not in the least,” Isolde remarked, raising the window shade. “The night is flawless, and dew will not form. Observe the moonlight.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0022 }

“I’m so happy that my window faces east toward the rising sun,” said Nell, walking across to Isolde. “It’s truly wonderful watching the morning emerge above those distant hills and shine through those pointed fir tops. Every morning it is brand new, and I feel as though my actual soul is washed in that stream of initial sunlight. Oh, Isolde, I cherish this small room so deeply. I cannot imagine how I will manage without it when I depart for town next month.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0023 }

“Please avoid mentioning that you are leaving this evening,” pleaded Isolde. “Thinking about it makes me feel extremely unhappy, and my desire is to enjoy myself tonight. What piece will you be reciting, Nell? Also, do you feel anxious?”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0024 }

“By no means. Having performed so many times before an audience, it doesn't bother me in the least anymore. My choice is to perform ‘The Maiden’s Vow.’ Its tone is very moving. A humorous piece will be performed by Laura Tranter, yet bringing tears to the audience appeals to me more than bringing laughter.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0025 }

“If you are encored, what will you recite?”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0026 }

“They will not even think about asking me for an encore,” sneered Nell, although she harbored her own private wishes that they might, and she was currently imagining recounting the entire affair to Obed when they sat down for breakfast the following day. “That must be Barney and Odette arriving—I can hear the carriage wheels. Let’s go.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0027 }

Barney Pullen demanded that Nell sit beside him on the front seat, causing her to climb up against her wishes. Sitting in the back with the girls would have been far more to her liking, as she could have chattered and laughed as much as she pleased. Barney possessed very little capacity for either chatter or laughter. Being a large, overweight, emotionless twenty-year-old lad, he had a round face devoid of expression and an agonizing inability to hold a conversation. Nevertheless, his admiration for Nell was vast, and the thought of traveling to Pale Sands accompanied by the slender, straight-backed figure at his side filled him with immense pride.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0028 }

Nell, through the effort of chatting behind her back to the girls and now and then tossing a courteous word to Barney—who smirked and laughed softly, never managing to devise an answer until the moment had passed—managed to take pleasure in the ride regardless of everything. The night was made for taking pleasure. The avenue swarmed with buggies, every single one heading toward the hotel, and laugher, pure as silver, reverberated again and again down its length. By the time they arrived at the hotel, light poured brilliantly from every floor. The women from the concert committee greeted them, and one of these ladies escorted Nell away to the performers' dressing room, a space packed with the members of a Port Marlow Symphony Club, in whose presence Nell abruptly experienced shyness, fear, and a sense of being rustic. Her gown, which had appeared so delicate and lovely inside the east gable, appeared basic and ordinary now—excessively basic and ordinary, it struck her, amid the numerous silks and laces shimmering and swishing all around her. How did her pearl beads measure up to the diamonds belonging to the large, striking woman beside her? Moreover, how pathetic her single tiny white rose had to appear next to the abundant hothouse blossoms worn by everyone else! Nell set her hat and jacket aside, cowering unhappily in a corner. She longed to be returned to the white room located at Grey Shutters.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0029 }

Her situation grew even more unpleasant when she shortly afterward reached the stage of the hotel’s large concert hall. Her eyes were blinded by the bright electric lamps, while she felt confused by the heavy fragrance and the drone of voices. She desired to be seated among the spectators alongside Isolde and Odette, who appeared to be enjoying themselves immensely far in the rear. Her position was compressed between a large woman wearing pink silk and a lofty, contemptuous young woman in a gown of white lace. Now and then, the large woman would pivot her head directly toward Nell to examine her through her eyeglasses, making Nell, who felt deeply bothered by this intense observation, feel as though a loud scream would burst from her; meanwhile, the young woman in white lace continuously remarked to the person beside her, loud enough to be heard, concerning the “country bumpkins” and “rustic belles” among the spectators, while lazily looking forward to “such fun” provided by the performances of area participants listed on the schedule. Nell felt certain that her hatred for that girl in the white-lace dress would last as long as she lived.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0030 }

It was bad luck for Nell that a hotel guest happened to be a professional elocutionist who had agreed to give a performance. This woman was supple, possessing dark eyes, and she wore an incredible dress made of a sparkling gray material that resembled woven moonbeams, along with jewels adorning her throat and her dark locks. Her voice possessed an extraordinary flexibility alongside an amazing expressive capacity, causing the spectators to react with extreme enthusiasm to her piece. For the moment, Nell paid no attention to herself or her difficulties, listening with entranced, glowing eyes; however, once the performance concluded, she abruptly covered her face using her hands. Standing up to recite after such an act was impossible for her—completely out of the question. Was it possible she had previously believed she possessed the ability to recite? Oh, how she wished to be back at Grey Shutters!
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0031 }

In this unfavorable instant, they called her name. Nell—who failed to see the somewhat guilty small jump of astonishment made by the girl in white lace, and who would not have grasped the delicate praise it suggested even if she had noticed—somehow rose, walking in a daze toward the front. Her face had grown so drained of color that, seated in the audience below, Isolde and Odette gripped one another's hands out of anxious empathy.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0032 }

A crushing wave of stage fright overwhelmed Nell. Although she had frequently given public recitations, an assembly like this had never confronted her before, and her energies were totally paralyzed by the vision of it. Every element—the lines of women wearing evening gowns, the discerning expressions, the entire environment of affluence and refinement surrounding her—proved exceedingly unfamiliar, dazzling, and disorienting. This contrasted sharply with the unadorned seating at the Debating Club, which was occupied by the familiar, kind expressions of acquaintances and townspeople. She believed these individuals would judge her without mercy. They probably expected entertainment from her “rustic” endeavors, just as the white-lace girl did. She experienced a feeling of shame and misery that was entirely beyond hope or help. A terrifying lightheadedness overtook her, her heart fluttered, and her knees shook; no speech could leave her mouth, and she would have escaped the stage the very next instant, notwithstanding the disgrace that she believed would permanently become her lot if she ran away.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0033 }

However, abruptly, while her wide, terrified eyes stared across the listeners, she spotted Hugh Carrow far at the rear of the hall, leaning frontward with a grin upon his countenance—a grin that appeared to Nell simultaneously victorious and mocking. Actually, it was not that at all. Hugh was simply grinning in admiration of the entire event overall, and specifically of the impression created by Nell’s slim white figure and ethereal face set before a backdrop of palms. Flossie Tulk, whom he had brought in his carriage, was seated next to him, and her expression truly was simultaneously victorious and mocking. Yet Nell failed to spot Flossie, and had she done so, she would not have minded. She sucked in a deep breath and threw her head backward with pride, bravery and resolve rushing through her like a jolt of electricity. She refused to falter in front of Hugh Carrow—he must not ever have the chance to mock her, not ever, not ever! Her terror and anxiety disappeared; and she commenced her performance, her distinct, lovely tone carrying to the most distant area of the hall with no shake or interruption. Composure had been entirely regained by her, and amid the bounce-back from that terrible instance of helplessness, she performed in a manner she had never achieved previously. As she concluded, there occurred explosions of genuine praise. Nell, moving backward toward her chair, turning red from modesty and joy, had her hand firmly gripped and moved by the heavy woman dressed in pink silk.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0034 }

“My dear, you performed wonderfully,” she gasped out. “I have been weeping like an infant, truly I have. Listen, they are calling for an encore—they will definitely make you return!”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0035 }

“Oh, I am unable to go,” Nell said in a state of confusion. “However—I have to, or else Obed is going to be disappointed. He stated that I would receive an encore from them.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0036 }

“In that case, ensure you do not let Obed down,” uttered the lady in pink, emitting a laugh.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0037 }

Wearing a smile and a blush, her eyes clear, Nell stepped back out and delivered an endearing, amusing short piece that charmed those listening even more. Her entire remaining evening proved to be a modest success.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0038 }

At the conclusion of the concert, the plump, rosy woman—the spouse of a wealthy American—escorted her around and presented her to all the guests, all of whom treated her with great kindness. The career reciter, Mrs. Evans, approached and conversed with her, remarking that her voice was delightful and that she “interpreted” her pieces marvellously. A faint, indifferent word of praise was even offered to her by the girl in white lace. In the grand, splendidly adorned dining hall, they ate supper; because they accompanied Nell, Isolde and Odette received an invitation to join in this meal as well, but Barney could not be located anywhere, having fled out of sheer dread of receiving a similar offer. Nevertheless, he was waiting for them alongside the team once everything had concluded, and the trio of girls stepped cheerfully outside into the peaceful, pale glow of the moonlight. Drawing a deep breath, Nell gazed up at the limpid sky past the shadowy branches of the fir trees.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0039 }

Ah, escaping once more into the night's untainted quiet felt truly wonderful! Everything possessed such vastness, stillness, and marvel, filled with the echoing hum of the ocean while the shadowy precipices past it resembled stern behemoths protecting spellbound shores.
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0040 }

“Wasn’t that an absolutely marvelous occasion?” Odette murmured, while they rode off. “If only I were a wealthy American who could pass the summer months residing in a hotel, donning gems and decollete gowns, and eating chicken salad along with ice cream each and every day. That must be vastly superior to working as a teacher. Your performance was truly wonderful, Nell, even though it initially seemed to me as if you would not start at all. It surpassed Mrs. Evans’s, in my opinion.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0041 }

“Oh, no, do not utter such remarks, Odette,” Nell said rapidly, “for it seems foolish. It could not possibly surpass Mrs. Evans’s, you see, since she works as a professional, whereas I am merely a schoolgirl possessing a slight talent for recitation. I am entirely content provided the audience simply enjoyed mine reasonably well.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0042 }

“Nell, I have a compliment to pass on to you,” Isolde remarked. “Considering the tone he used, I am fairly sure it has to be a compliment. In any case, a portion of it was. Directly behind Odette and myself sat an American—a man who looked so romantic, possessing coal-black hair together with eyes of the same shade. According to Flossie Tulk, he is an eminent artist, and the cousin of her mother in Boston has married a man who formerly attended school alongside him. Anyhow, we overheard him remarking—isn't that right, Odette?—‘Which girl is that on the platform with the magnificent Titian hair? Her face is one I would love to paint.’ So there you are, Nell. However, what is the meaning of Titian hair?”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0043 }

“If it is translated, it stands for simple red, I suppose,” Nell giggled. “Titian was an extremely renowned painter who enjoyed portraying women with red hair.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0044 }

“Were you looking at every one of the diamonds worn by those ladies?” Odette asked with a sigh. “They shone so brightly. Wouldn’t you girls adore being wealthy?”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0045 }

“We are rich,” Nell stated firmly. “Why, sixteen years stand to our credit, and we enjoy the happiness of queens, and imaginations belong to all of us, to one degree or another. Direct your gaze to that sea, girls—entirely composed of silver, shadow, and visions of unseen things. Having millions of dollars and strands of diamonds would not enable us to appreciate its beauty any further. You would refuse to transform into any of those women if the choice were yours. Would it be your desire to become that white-lace girl, bearing a bitter expression throughout your existence, as though your very birth occurred with your nose turned up at everything? Or the pink lady, pleasant and good-natured though she may be, yet so heavy and low of stature that a figure is truly lacking? Or even Mrs. Evans, possessing that deeply, deeply sorrowful expression within her eyes? A terrible unhappiness must have befallen her at some point to produce such an expression. You know you would not, Odette Pullen!”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0046 }

“I am not sure—precisely,” Odette stated without conviction. “My belief is that a person would find much solace in diamonds.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0047 }

“Well, I have no desire to be anybody other than myself, even should I remain unsoothed by diamonds for the rest of my days,” Nell announced. “Being Nell of Grey Shutters suits me fine, along with my pearl bead strand. I am certain that Obed bestowed just as much affection upon me through them as was ever attached to Madame the Pink Lady’s gems.”
{: #nw-v01-c33-p0048 }
